  const Sn = 0, Qs = 1, vn = 2, zg = 4, Rg = 4, _g = 4, Og = 4, Fg = 4, Ng = 4, kx = `
/**
 * How far off its own plane a decal will still paint, in metres, ASYMMETRICALLY.
 *
 * Generous downward and tight upward, and the asymmetry is the whole design:
 *
 * - DOWN is the bug this exists for. The terrain re-meshes at coarser LODs as
 *   the camera rises, and a LOD-3 chunk has been measured drawing its surface
 *   2.4 m above its own collider \u2014 so the ground a mark was laid on can fall
 *   away by metres without the mark being wrong.
 * - UP is occlusion. A decal draws after the depth test, so this test is the
 *   only thing stopping it painting on whatever stands over it, and a hull, a
 *   wheel or a player is always ABOVE the ground its mark is on.
 *
 * When the ground rises through a mark instead, the mark is rejected and
 * disappears. That is the deliberate trade: a track that vanishes reads as the
 * terrain having changed, and a track that floats in mid-air reads as a bug \u2014
 * which is what it was reported as, six times.
 */
#define DECAL_BELOW 3.0
#define DECAL_ABOVE 0.35
`, bR = `
${kx}
attribute vec4 aBirth;
attribute vec4 aMotion;
attribute vec4 aShape;
attribute vec4 aTint;
attribute vec4 aForce;
attribute vec4 aCurve;

uniform float uTime;

/**
 * How fast the noise field slides past a FIXED emitter, in cells per second.
 *
 * The field is coherent in space, which is what makes a cloud form lobes instead
 * of speckle. For a source that moves, position does that work. For one that does
 * not \u2014 a chimney \u2014 position is constant and this is the only thing separating
 * one puff from the next.
 *
 * It was 0.9, which moves the sample half a cell a second: at a hundred-odd puffs
 * a second, dozens in a row shared a drift direction and that direction then
 * swung smoothly. Slow, correlated and directional is the signature of WIND, and
 * that is what it looked like after the wind was removed. 6 decorrelates a plume
 * within a few tenths of a second, which reads as billowing rather than waving,
 * and is still slow enough that neighbours born together stay together.
 */
const float TURBULENCE_DRIFT = 6.0;

varying vec4 vTint;
varying vec2 vUv;
varying float vViewDepth;

#ifdef USE_DECAL
	/** How far the quad had to move, along the ground normal, to reach the
	 *  surface the frame drew. Signed: up is something standing on the mark. */
	varying float vRise;

	// The frame's own depth, sampled at VERTEX rate \u2014 see the snap below.
	uniform sampler2D uDepth;
	uniform vec2 uProjToView;
	uniform vec2 uProjScale;
#endif

#include <common>
#include <fog_pars_vertex>

// Hash-based value noise, the cheap standard one. Aperiodic, non-separable, and
// smooth: neighbouring positions give neighbouring answers, which is what makes
// the cloud form lobes instead of speckle.
vec3 hash33(vec3 p) {
	p = vec3(dot(p, vec3(127.1, 311.7, 74.7)), dot(p, vec3(269.5, 183.3, 246.1)), dot(p, vec3(113.5, 271.9, 124.6)));
	return fract(sin(p) * 43758.5453123) * 2.0 - 1.0;
}

vec3 turbulentDrift(vec3 p) {
	vec3 scaled = p * 0.55;
	vec3 cell = floor(scaled);
	vec3 f = fract(scaled);
	// Smoothstep weights, so the field has no visible cell edges.
	vec3 w = f * f * (3.0 - 2.0 * f);

	vec3 x00 = mix(hash33(cell + vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)), hash33(cell + vec3(1.0, 0.0, 0.0)), w.x);
	vec3 x10 = mix(hash33(cell + vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0)), hash33(cell + vec3(1.0, 1.0, 0.0)), w.x);
	vec3 x01 = mix(hash33(cell + vec3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0)), hash33(cell + vec3(1.0, 0.0, 1.0)), w.x);
	vec3 x11 = mix(hash33(cell + vec3(0.0, 1.0, 1.0)), hash33(cell + vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0)), w.x);

	return mix(mix(x00, x10, w.y), mix(x01, x11, w.y), w.z);
}

void main() {
	float age = uTime - aBirth.w;
	float life = aMotion.w;
	float u = age / life;

	// Dead, unborn, or never written: collapse to a degenerate point outside
	// clip space. The vertex is still shaded, which is the cost of not having a
	// CPU-side free list, but no fragment is ever generated \u2014 and a fragment is
	// what actually costs on the machines this has to run on. A never-written
	// slot has life 0, so u is +inf or NaN and the same branch catches it.
	if (!(u >= 0.0 && u < 1.0)) {
		gl_Position = vec4(2.0, 2.0, 2.0, 1.0);
		vTint = vec4(0.0);
		vUv = vec2(0.0);
		vViewDepth = 0.0;
		#ifdef USE_DECAL
			vRise = 0.0;
		#endif
		return;
	}

	// Ballistic travel with linear drag, integrated in closed form.
	//
	//   v(t) = v0 * exp(-k t)   ->   p(t) = p0 + v0 * (1 - exp(-k t)) / k
	//
	// The k -> 0 limit of that fraction is t, and the expression is 0/0 there,
	// so it is branched rather than left to produce a NaN that would take the
	// particle to nowhere. Gravity is added undamped: a drag-damped gravity term
	// is a second exponential for an effect nobody can see over a particle's
	// lifetime, and keeping it linear-in-t-squared is what lets the whole motion
	// stay one line. The sign is along +Y: negative falls, positive is buoyancy,
	// which is how smoke and fine dust rise.
	// A MARK does not move at all: it is scratched into the ground where the
	// wheel was and stays there. That is also what frees aMotion to carry the
	// ground normal for it \u2014 a static particle has no velocity to store.
	vec3 center;
	if (aCurve.w > 0.5) {
		center = aBirth.xyz;
	} else {
		float k = aForce.x;
		float travel = k > 1e-4 ? (1.0 - exp(-k * age)) / k : age;
		center = aBirth.xyz + aMotion.xyz * travel + vec3(0.0, 0.5 * aForce.y * age * age, 0.0);
	}

	// TURBULENCE \u2014 a frozen, aperiodic field, sampled once per particle at BIRTH.
	//
	// Drag kills the launch velocity in about half a second, and after that every
	// particle in a trail feels identical forces, so the cloud freezes in the
	// shape it had at 0.5 s: the line its births were laid on. Real dust keeps
	// being pulled apart, and its width grows without bound.
	//
	// Two properties this has to have, and the version before it had neither:
	//
	// NO AGE TERM. Age inside the field makes each particle oscillate with the
	// field period, so the trail waves back and forth \u2014 a standing wave, worst
	// near the wheel where the phase moves fastest. Turbulent displacement is a
	// random WALK: it accumulates along a direction and does not come back.
	//
	// APERIODIC AND NOT SEPARABLE. A sum of sines is both, and it shows: for a
	// machine driving along one axis every wheel shares the same x term and
	// differs only by a constant, so all four trails undulate in step and each
	// repeats every few metres. Nick saw exactly that \u2014 every wheel moving the
	// same way. Hash noise has no period to find and no axis to share.
	//
	// Sampled at the birth POSITION rather than per particle, so neighbours born
	// centimetres apart drift together and the cloud separates into lobes.
	// Per-particle jitter fuzzes the edge of a line and leaves a line.
	// Airborne only. A mark is stuck to the ground it was made on: drifting it
	// makes the whole trail crawl sideways as it fades, which reads as the world
	// sliding rather than as dust moving.
	if (aCurve.w < 0.5) {
		// Sampled at the birth position AND the birth TIME.
		//
		// Position alone is coherent, which is right for a trail laid across the
		// ground and wrong for a source that does not move: every particle from a
		// standing chimney is born at the same point, samples the same eddy, and
		// the whole plume leans one fixed way. That is indistinguishable from wind
		// \u2014 and it was still there after the wind was removed.
		//
		// Birth time is CONSTANT per particle, so this decorrelates consecutive
		// puffs without making any single one oscillate. Physically it is the
		// eddies drifting past the nozzle, which is what they do.
		vec3 swirl = turbulentDrift(aBirth.xyz + vec3(aBirth.w * TURBULENCE_DRIFT));
		center += swirl * aCurve.z * age;

	}

	float size = mix(aShape.x, aShape.y, u);

	// A MARK DOES NOT SPIN. Its orientation is the direction the wheel was going
	// and that does not change once it is scratched into the ground.
	//
	// This is not a precaution, it is a fix: aShape.z is the spin RATE in the
	// shared formula, and a mark stores its HEADING there \u2014 so every mark was
	// turning at its own heading in radians per second. Anything a mark reuses
	// from the airborne layout has to be read only inside the flat branch.
	float rot = aCurve.w > 0.5 ? 0.0 : aShape.w + aShape.z * age;
	float c = cos(rot);
	float s = sin(rot);
	vec2 corner = position.xy * size;
	vec2 spun = vec2(corner.x * c - corner.y * s, corner.x * s + corner.y * c);

	vec4 mv;
	if (aCurve.w > 0.5) {
		// FLAT: the quad lies in the plane of the GROUND, not the world's XZ
		// plane. Those are the same thing only where the ground is level \u2014 on a
		// hillside a world-flat quad cuts through the slope and half of it stands
		// clear of the terrain, which is the trail visibly lifting off the ground
		// as you crest a hill.
		//
		// The normal arrives in aMotion.xyz. A mark does not move, so its velocity
		// slot is free, and reusing it costs nothing where another attribute would
		// cost sixteen bytes on every particle in the world.
		vec3 n = normalize(aMotion.xyz);

		// Along the direction of TRAVEL, not an arbitrary tangent. A mark is a
		// streak the wheel drew, so its long axis is the path it took; a quad
		// oriented any other way is a blob that happens to lie flat. The heading
		// rides in aShape.z, which is the spin rate a mark has no use for.
		vec3 heading = vec3(cos(aShape.z), 0.0, sin(aShape.z));
		vec3 tangent = heading - n * dot(n, heading);
		float tl = length(tangent);
		tangent = tl > 1e-4 ? tangent / tl : normalize(cross(n, vec3(1.0, 0.0, 0.0)));
		vec3 bitangent = cross(n, tangent);

		// Longer than it is wide: aForce.w carries the aspect, which for an
		// airborne particle is unused.
		center += tangent * (spun.x * aForce.w) + bitangent * spun.y;
		mv = modelViewMatrix * vec4(center, 1.0);

		#ifdef USE_DECAL
			/**
			 * WHAT IS ACTUALLY BEHIND THIS CORNER.
			 *
			 * A mark used to be a quad at the height the ground had when the wheel
			 * passed, drawn with the world and depth-tested. The terrain does not
			 * stay there: a chunk re-meshed at a coarser LOD draws its surface
			 * metres from where it was \u2014 measured at 2.4 m for LOD 3 \u2014 so marks
			 * laid correctly end up standing clear of the hill once you jump one.
			 * Five attempts at the PLACEMENT failed because the placement was
			 * right and the ground moved.
			 *
			 * So a mark stops being a thing in the world and becomes paint on the
			 * picture, applied after the composite where the frame's depth is
			 * readable. Each corner asks what the frame drew behind it, and the
			 * answer, as a height above the mark's own plane, is all the fragment
			 * stage needs to decide whether that is ground worth marking. Per
			 * VERTEX: four texture fetches for a mark, where searching for the
			 * surface per PIXEL would mean widening every quad to cover wherever
			 * the ground might have gone \u2014 a hundred times the fill, on a
			 * thousand live marks at speed.
			 */
			vec4 clip = projectionMatrix * mv;
			vec2 snapUv = clip.xy / clip.w * 0.5 + 0.5;
			float rawZ = texture2D(uDepth, clamp(snapUv, 0.0, 1.0)).x;

			bool inFrame = clip.w > 0.0 &&
				snapUv.x == clamp(snapUv.x, 0.0, 1.0) && snapUv.y == clamp(snapUv.y, 0.0, 1.0);

			if (inFrame && rawZ < 1.0) {
				float dist = uProjToView.y / (rawZ * 2.0 - 1.0 - uProjToView.x);
				vec3 surface = vec3(clip.xy / clip.w * uProjScale, -1.0) * dist;
				vRise = dot(surface - mv.xyz, normalize(mat3(modelViewMatrix) * n));
			} else if (inFrame) {
				// Sky over a cliff edge. There is nothing to mark, and a track
				// hanging in mid-air over a drop is the exact picture this was
				// reported as six times.
				vRise = 1e4;
			} else {
				/*
				 * OFF SCREEN IS NO ANSWER, NOT A NO.
				 *
				 * The depth buffer only covers the frame, so a corner projecting
				 * outside it has nothing to say about the ground there. Treating it
				 * as "no ground" \u2014 which it was, sharing the reject with sky \u2014
				 * discarded the mark, and vRise is a VARYING, so a quad with one
				 * corner past the edge interpolates toward the reject across its
				 * whole width. Every track faded out and cut off approaching the
				 * border of the screen, worst at the bottom where the marks are
				 * nearest and their quads largest in screen space.
				 *
				 * With no answer available, the mark's own placement is the best
				 * information there is \u2014 and it is the placement that was correct
				 * all along, everywhere except across a LOD change. So a mark at
				 * the frame's edge draws where the wheel put it, which is what it
				 * did before any of this projection existed.
				 */
				vRise = 0.0;
			}
		#endif

	} else {
		// Billboard in VIEW space, which is what makes the quad face the camera
		// without a per-particle matrix: the offset is applied after the view
		// transform, so it is always parallel to the screen.
		mv = modelViewMatrix * vec4(center, 1.0);
		mv.xy += spun;
	}

	// Fade in over the head of the life, out over the tail. Both are fractions
	// of the life rather than seconds so an effect reads the same however long
	// its particles live.
	float fadeIn = aCurve.x > 0.0 ? smoothstep(0.0, aCurve.x, u) : 1.0;
	float fadeOut = aCurve.y > 0.0 ? 1.0 - smoothstep(1.0 - aCurve.y, 1.0, u) : 1.0;

	vTint = vec4(aTint.rgb, aTint.a * fadeIn * fadeOut);
	vUv = position.xy + 0.5;
	vViewDepth = -mv.z;

	vec4 mvPosition = mv;
	gl_Position = projectionMatrix * mv;

	#include <fog_vertex>
}
`, SR = `
precision highp float;
${kx}

uniform sampler2D uAtlas;

uniform sampler2D uDepth;
uniform vec2 uResolution;
uniform vec2 uProjToView;
uniform float uSoftFade;

varying vec4 vTint;
varying vec2 vUv;
varying float vViewDepth;

#ifdef USE_DECAL
	/** How far the quad had to move, along the ground normal, to reach the
	 *  surface the frame drew. Signed: up is something standing on the mark. */
	varying float vRise;
#endif

#include <common>
#include <fog_pars_fragment>

void main() {
	vec4 color = vTint;

	// Where on the MARK this pixel is. The quad's own uv when the mark is placed;
	// recomputed from the real surface when it is projected.
	vec2 markUv = vUv;

	#ifdef USE_DECAL
		/**
		 * Reject what the snap could not handle.
		 *
		 * The band first: how far a corner had to travel to reach the surface, and
		 * which way. Down is the terrain having re-meshed under a mark, which is
		 * the whole point and is allowed generously. UP is something STANDING on
		 * the mark \u2014 a hull, a wheel, a player \u2014 and a decal has no depth test to
		 * refuse it with, so this is the refusal.
		 */
		if (vRise > DECAL_ABOVE || vRise < -DECAL_BELOW) discard;

		// And per pixel, whatever is nearer than the surface the quad settled on.
		// The band is measured at four corners; this catches the rock covering
		// half a mark, which the corners can miss entirely.
		float sceneZ = texture2D(uDepth, gl_FragCoord.xy / uResolution).x * 2.0 - 1.0;
		if (uProjToView.y / (sceneZ - uProjToView.x) < vViewDepth - 0.05) discard;
		#endif

	#ifdef USE_MARK
		// A MARK, not a puff lying down.
		//
		// Dust is a soft radial blob; a scuff in the ground is a streak with a
		// defined edge across its width, a soft one along its length, and torn
		// breakup inside it \u2014 grass does not flatten evenly. Sharing the disc is
		// what made the marks read as dust pressed flat.
		vec2 d = (markUv - 0.5) * 2.0;
		// No edge and no flat core, ACROSS the mark especially.
		//
		// A smoothstep leaves a defined rim, and a decal is drawn after the
		// composite where nothing softens it afterwards \u2014 no TAA, no soft-particle
		// fade \u2014 so that rim survives to the screen as a crisp line and a track
		// reads as two drawn stripes. An exponential falloff has no rim to survive,
		// which is what lets the band sit in the grass instead of on top of it.
		float across = exp(-2.2 * d.y * d.y);
		float along = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.3, 1.0, abs(d.x));
		// Breakup, not texture: at full strength the grain itself reads as an edge.
		float grain = 0.86 + 0.14 * sin(markUv.x * 37.0 + markUv.y * 23.0) * sin(markUv.y * 41.0);
		color.a *= across * along * grain;
	#elif defined(USE_ATLAS)
		color *= texture2D(uAtlas, vUv);
	#else
		// A gaussian-ish puff, so the system draws convincing dust and smoke
		// before any art exists.
		//
		// The falloff matters more than it sounds. A disc with a defined edge \u2014
		// a smoothstep with a flat core \u2014 reads as a BLOB, and a trail of them
		// reads as a row of blobs however densely you pack them, because the eye
		// finds the repeated silhouette. An exponential falloff has no edge and
		// no flat core, so overlapping puffs sum into one cloud instead of
		// stacking into lumps.
		float d = length(vUv - 0.5) * 2.0;
		color.a *= exp(-4.5 * d * d) * step(d, 1.0);
	#endif

	#ifdef USE_SOFT
		// Fade against whatever is already in the depth buffer. Both depths are
		// converted to view space first: a difference of raw non-linear depth
		// values is meaningless as a distance, and using it directly makes the
		// fade distance change with how far away the particle is.
		vec2 screenUv = gl_FragCoord.xy / uResolution;
		float sceneDepth = texture2D(uDepth, screenUv).x;
		// Both POSITIVE distances along the view ray: vViewDepth is -mv.z, and
		// this reconstruction is the same expression the decal band compares
		// against it directly. So the gap is scene minus particle. Negating it
		// made every gap negative and discarded every soft particle \u2014 never seen,
		// because nothing enabled this define until the smoke moved past the
		// composite and needed it for occlusion.
		float sceneView = uProjToView.y / (sceneDepth * 2.0 - 1.0 - uProjToView.x);
		float gap = sceneView - vViewDepth;
		color.a *= clamp(gap / uSoftFade, 0.0, 1.0);
	#endif

	if (color.a <= 0.001) discard;

	gl_FragColor = color;
	#include <fog_fragment>

	#ifdef USE_DISPLAY_OUTPUT
		/*
		 * Drawn AFTER the composite, so nothing downstream will encode this.
		 *
		 * The composite is what turns the forward pass's linear radiance into the
		 * sRGB the screen shows. A field drawn past it writes straight to a
		 * display-referred image, and a linear value shown as if it were already
		 * encoded is far too dark \u2014 0.2 linear should leave as 0.48, not 0.2. So
		 * this does the composite's own encode, the piecewise sRGB curve rather
		 * than pow(1/2.2), because the two disagree exactly in the deep shadows
		 * that smoke is made of.
		 */
		gl_FragColor.rgb = mix(
			gl_FragColor.rgb * 12.92,
			1.055 * pow(max(gl_FragColor.rgb, 0.0), vec3(1.0 / 2.4)) - 0.055,
			step(vec3(0.0031308), gl_FragColor.rgb)
		);
	#endif
}

  const ff = 10, IN = 0.67, Ey = 2, TN = [
    0.5058824,
    0.6509804,
    0.67058825
  ], kN = [
    0.7058824,
    0.8235294,
    0.49411765

void main() {
	vEyeRay = position;
	gl_Position = projectionMatrix * modelViewMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0);

`, WN = `
precision highp float;

uniform vec3 uSunDir;
uniform vec3 uSunFogColor;
uniform vec3 uFogColor;
uniform float uProbePass;

in vec3 vEyeRay;
out vec4 outColor;

const vec3 INV_WAVELENGTH = vec3(${kt(ku[0])}, ${kt(ku[1])}, ${kt(ku[2])});
const vec3 GROUND_LINEAR = vec3(${kt(Tu[0])}, ${kt(Tu[1])}, ${kt(Tu[2])});

// Optical depth along a ray leaving the atmosphere at this angle. The quartic is
// the standard closed-form fit to the integral \u2014 evaluating it properly per
// sample would cost more than the entire rest of the shader.
float scaleAngle(float inCos) {
	float x = 1.0 - inCos;
	float poly = 0.459 + x * (3.83 + x * (-6.80 + x * 5.25));
	return 0.25 * exp(-0.00287 + x * poly);
}

float rayleighPhase(vec3 light, vec3 ray) {
	float eyeCos = dot(light, ray);
	return 0.75 + 0.75 * eyeCos * eyeCos;
}

float miePhase(float eyeCos, float eyeCos2) {
	float temp = (1.0 + ${kt(Iu)}) - (2.0 * ${kt(FN)}) * eyeCos;
	temp = pow(max(temp, 1.0e-4), ${kt(BN)});
	return ${kt(1.5 * ((1 - Iu) / (2 + Iu)))} * (1.0 + eyeCos2) / temp;
}

void main() {
	vec3 eyeRay = normalize(vEyeRay);
	vec3 sunDir = normalize(uSunDir);
	vec3 cameraPos = vec3(0.0, ${kt(ha + Bi)}, 0.0);
	vec3 kr4 = INV_WAVELENGTH * ${kt(LN)} + ${kt(ON)};

	vec3 cIn = vec3(0.0);
	vec3 cOut = vec3(0.0);

	if (eyeRay.y >= 0.0) {
		// Looking at sky: integrate along the ray to where it leaves the shell.
		float far = sqrt(${kt(_N)} + eyeRay.y * eyeRay.y - 1.0) - eyeRay.y;
		float startAngle = dot(eyeRay, cameraPos) / ${kt(ha + Bi)};
		float startOffset = scaleAngle(startAngle) * ${kt(Math.exp(Au * -Bi))};

		float sampleLength = far / 2.0;
		float scaledLength = sampleLength * ${kt(pd)};
		vec3 sampleRay = eyeRay * sampleLength;
		vec3 samplePoint = cameraPos + sampleRay * 0.5;
		vec3 frontColor = vec3(0.0);

		// Two samples, unrolled. A third buys almost nothing at this thickness.
		for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
			float height = length(samplePoint);
			float depth = exp(${kt(Au)} * (${kt(ha)} - height));
			float lightAngle = dot(sunDir, samplePoint) / height;
			float cameraAngle = dot(eyeRay, samplePoint) / height;
			float scatter = startOffset + depth * (scaleAngle(lightAngle) - scaleAngle(cameraAngle));
			vec3 attenuate = exp(-clamp(scatter, 0.0, ${kt(Iy)}) * kr4);
			frontColor += attenuate * (depth * scaledLength);
			samplePoint += sampleRay;
		}

		cIn = frontColor * (INV_WAVELENGTH * ${kt(ky)});
		cOut = frontColor * ${kt(Ty)};
	} else {
		// Looking below the horizon: a single sample down to the ground plane.
		float far = ${kt(-Bi)} / min(-0.001, eyeRay.y);
		vec3 pos = cameraPos + eyeRay * far;
		float cameraScale = scaleAngle(dot(-eyeRay, pos));
		float lightScale = scaleAngle(dot(sunDir, pos));
		float cameraOffset = cameraScale * ${kt(Math.exp(-Bi / b1))};

		float sampleLength = far / 2.0;
		float scaledLength = sampleLength * ${kt(pd)};
		vec3 samplePoint = cameraPos + eyeRay * sampleLength * 0.5;

		float height = length(samplePoint);
		float depth = exp(${kt(Au)} * (${kt(ha)} - height));
		float scatter = depth * (lightScale + cameraScale) - cameraOffset;
		vec3 attenuate = exp(-clamp(scatter, 0.0, ${kt(Iy)}) * kr4);
		vec3 frontColor = attenuate * (depth * scaledLength);

		cIn = frontColor * (INV_WAVELENGTH * ${kt(ky)} + ${kt(Ty)});
		cOut = clamp(attenuate, 0.0, 1.0);
	}

	vec3 groundColor = (cIn + GROUND_LINEAR * cOut) * ${kt(Ey)};
	vec3 skyColor = cIn * rayleighPhase(sunDir, -eyeRay) * ${kt(Ey)};
	vec3 sunColor = clamp(cOut, 0.0, 1.0) * ${kt(DN)};

	float y = -eyeRay.y / ${kt(NN)};
	vec3 col = mix(skyColor, groundColor, clamp(y, 0.0, 1.0));

	// The sun disc is dropped while baking a reflection probe: a mirrored disc
	// punches a moving hot spot through every glossy surface in the world.
	if (y < 0.0 && uProbePass < 0.5) {
		float focusedEyeCos = pow(clamp(dot(sunDir, eyeRay), 0.0, 1.0), ${kt(zN)});
		col += sunColor * miePhase(-focusedEyeCos, focusedEyeCos * focusedEyeCos);
	}

	// Horizon fog band, tinted toward the sun. This is what makes the dome sit
	// in the same air as the terrain rather than behind it.
	float fogT = clamp((eyeRay.y - ${kt(Ay)}) / ${kt(RN - Ay)}, 0.0, 1.0);
	float fogAmount = 1.0 - (fogT * fogT * (3.0 - 2.0 * fogT));
	vec3 sunFog = pow(uSunFogColor, vec3(2.2));
	vec3 fogTarget = mix(uFogColor, sunFog, clamp(dot(eyeRay, uSunDir), 0.0, 1.0));
	col = mix(col, fogTarget, fogAmount);

	outColor = vec4(col, 1.0);
}
`;

  function Py(i, t) {

				// a soft band rather than a hard step so the boundary reads cleanly.

      const { startAbove: o, reachBelow: r } = di, a = t.minX - wn, l = t.minZ - wn + e * wn;
      for (let c = 0; c < zo; c++) {
        const u = a + c * wn, h = ls(this.ground.field, u, l), f = s(u, l, h + o, h - r, h);
        n.heights[e * zo + c] = f ?? Number.NaN, f !== null ? n.any = true : n.gaps = true;
      }
    }
    upload(t, e, s, n, o, r, a) {
      const l = this.scratchGeometry;
      l.setAttribute("position", new gt(s.root.subarray(n * 3, o * 3), 3)), l.setAttribute("aOffset", new gt(s.offset.subarray(n * 3, o * 3), 3, true)), l.setAttribute("aData", new gt(s.data.subarray(n * 4, o * 4), 4, true)), l.setIndex(new gt(s.index.subarray(r, a), 1)), this.mesh.setGeometryAt(t, l), this.mesh.setVisibleAt(e, o > n), this.mesh.setColorAt(e, this.bornColour);
    }
    finish(t, e) {
      const s = this.flights.get(t);
      if (!s) return;
      this.flights.delete(t);
      const n = (this.generations.get(t) ?? 0) !== s.generation, o = this.tileDistance(s.tx, s.tz) >= this.range + $t + Po;
      if (n || o) {
        s.slotClass.free.push(s.slot);
        return;
      }
      const r = s.slot, a = e.bounds, l = this.scratchBox;
      l.min.set(a[0], a[1], a[2]), l.max.set(a[3], a[4], a[5]), l.getBoundingSphere(this.scratchSphere);
      const c = this.tiles.get(t), u = c ? c.born : s.instant ? this.uTime.value - e0 : this.uTime.value;
      this.bornColour.setRGB(u, 0, 0, ui);
      const h = e.placed * Qo, f = e.placed * Ks;
      this.upload(r.geometryId, r.instanceId, e, 0, h, 0, f), r.extraGeometryId >= 0 && this.upload(r.extraGeometryId, r.extraInstanceId, e, h, e.root.length / 3, f, e.index.length), c && this.release(c);
      const d = {
        key: t,
        tx: s.tx,
        tz: s.tz,
        builtAt: s.builtAt,
        keep: e.dropped > 0 ? e.ranks[e.placed - 1] / 255 : s.keep,
        truncated: e.dropped > 0,
        cards: s.slotClass.cards,
        slotClass: s.slotClass,
        slot: r,
        blades: e.placed,
        roots: e.roots,
        ranks: e.ranks,
        drawn: e.index.length,
        box: new Je(new z(a[0], a[1], a[2]), new z(a[3], a[4], a[5])),
        stale: false,
        born: u,
        gaps: s.gaps ? ((c == null ? void 0 : c.gaps) ?? 0) + 1 : 0,
        builtTime: this.uTime.value
      };
      this.tiles.set(t, d), this.trimDraw(d), e.dropped > 0 && (this.bandCheckX = Number.NaN);
    }
    get instanceCount() {
      let t = 0;
      for (const e of this.tiles.values()) t += e.blades;
      return t;
    }
    get stats() {
      const t = se.map(() => 0);
      let e = 0, s = 0;
      for (const n of this.tiles.values()) t[this.bandOf(n)] += n.blades, e += n.blades * n.cards * Ks, s += n.drawn;
      return {
        resident: this.tiles.size,
        pending: this.pending.length + (this.prep === null ? 0 : 1),
        inFlight: this.flights.size,
        instances: this.instanceCount,
        perBand: t,
        bakedTriangles: e / 3,
        drawnTriangles: s / 3
      };
    }
    bandOf(t) {
      const e = this.tileDistance(t.tx, t.tz);
      for (let s = 0; s < se.length; s++) if (e < se[s].radius) return s;
      return se.length - 1;
    }
    get packed() {
      const t = this.instanceCount, e = new Float32Array(t * 3), s = new Uint8Array(t);
      let n = 0;
      for (const o of this.tiles.values()) e.set(o.roots, n * 3), s.fill(this.bandOf(o), n, n + o.blades), n += o.blades;
      return {
        root: e,
        band: s,
        count: t
      };
    }
  }
  const gd = 8e3, QD = `
varying vec2 vUv;
void main() {
  vUv = uv;
  gl_Position = vec4(position.xy, 0.0, 1.0);
}
`, JD = `
uniform sampler2D uSource;
varying vec2 vUv;
void main() {
  gl_FragColor = texture2D(uSource, vUv);
}
`, tL = `
#include <fog_pars_vertex>
varying vec3 vWorldPos;

void main() {
  // Flat plane \u2014 the sea surface never moves vertically. All wave motion is
  // faked in the fragment via animated ripple normals (glint/sparkle/foam).
  vec4 world = modelMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0);
  vWorldPos = world.xyz;
  vec4 mvPosition = viewMatrix * world;
  #include <fog_vertex>
  gl_Position = projectionMatrix * mvPosition;
}
`, eL = `
precision highp float;

uniform sampler2D uHeightmap;
uniform float uTerrainSize;
uniform float uWaterLevel;
uniform vec3 uSunDir;
uniform vec3 uSunColor;
uniform vec3 uShallow;
uniform vec3 uDeep;
uniform vec3 uSkyColor;
uniform vec3 uSubsurface;
uniform sampler2D uScene;
uniform vec2 uSceneTexel;
uniform float uTime;

#include <fog_pars_fragment>
varying vec3 vWorldPos;

float seabed(vec2 xz) {
  vec2 uv = xz / uTerrainSize + 0.5;
  return texture2D(uHeightmap, uv).r;
}

void main() {
  vec2 xz = vWorldPos.xz;
  float depth = uWaterLevel - seabed(xz);
  if (depth <= 0.0) discard;

  // Anti-aliased waterline: coverage ramps over ~1 px around depth = 0 using
  // fwidth(depth). Crisp and stable on every shore angle \u2014 fwidth adapts to how
  // fast depth changes per pixel \u2014 so the edge neither jaggies nor jitters, and
  // (unlike a depth-based fade) never widens into a smear on shallow coasts.
  // fwidth explodes once a pixel spans many metres of seabed, so the coverage
  // term flickers at range; past the LOD fade the surface is solid anyway.
  float edge = clamp(depth / max(fwidth(depth), 1e-4), 0.0, 1.0);

  // Horizontal distance to the shoreline = depth / seabed slope. Driving the
  // foam off this instead of raw depth keeps it a constant world-space width
  // no matter how gently the seabed slopes: a depth-based band stretches into a
  // wide smear wherever land and water meet at a shallow angle. The slope comes
  // from a central difference of the seabed height (clamped away from zero so a
  // dead-flat seabed can't blow the distance up to infinity).
  float e = 3.0;
  float gx = seabed(xz + vec2(e, 0.0)) - seabed(xz - vec2(e, 0.0));
  float gz = seabed(xz + vec2(0.0, e)) - seabed(xz - vec2(0.0, e));
  float slope = max(length(vec2(gx, gz)) / (2.0 * e), 1e-3);
  float shoreDist = depth / slope;

  // Surface normal: a cheap two-octave ripple, no textures and no vertex work.
  //
  // Waves are deliberately out of scope here, but a mirror-flat plane is the
  // single biggest tell that water is fake \u2014 the sun glint becomes a hard disc
  // and the sky reflection a mirror. Perturbing the NORMAL alone buys most of
  // the life of a wavy surface for a few ALU: the surface stays geometrically
  // flat (so nothing else has to change) while the lighting behaves as if it
  // were not.
  // Four octaves, each rotated and drifting its own way.
  //
  // Two sines at one scale is the tell: water reads as water because the same
  // shape repeats at every size at once, and any single frequency gives a
  // regular corduroy. Photon and Bliss both isolate this into their own
  // water_normal stage for the same reason \u2014 the normal IS the look on a flat
  // surface. Each octave is rotated by an irrational-ish angle so the layers
  // never line up into a grid, and each drifts at its own speed so no beat
  // frequency emerges.
  vec2 ripple = vec2(0.0);
  float amp = 0.052;
  float freq = 0.035;
  float phase = uTime;
  for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
    // 2.4 radians per octave: a bad rational multiple of pi, so four layers
    // cannot share an axis.
    float a = float(i) * 2.4;
    vec2 dir = vec2(cos(a), sin(a));
    vec2 q = vec2(dot(xz, dir), dot(xz, vec2(-dir.y, dir.x))) * freq;

    // The crest sharpening every stylised water shader uses: sin() alone is too
    // round, so bias it toward its peaks. Cheap, and it is what gives the
    // surface glinting ridges instead of soft bumps.
    float w = sin(q.x + phase * 0.7) * cos(q.y * 1.17 - phase * 0.45);
    ripple += dir * (w * abs(w)) * amp;

    amp *= 0.55;
    freq *= 2.17;
    phase *= 1.35;
  }

  // Flatten the ripple with distance, or it aliases into shimmer at the horizon
  // \u2014 the same reason a normal map needs mips.
  float viewDist = length(cameraPosition - vWorldPos);
  ripple *= exp(-viewDist * 0.004);

  vec3 n = normalize(vec3(ripple.x, 1.0, ripple.y));
  vec3 viewDir = normalize(cameraPosition - vWorldPos);

  // Underside: the camera is below the surface and looking up through it.
  //
  // Without this the plane shades as if seen from above from both sides, which
  // is what makes a half-submerged shot fall apart \u2014 the top half looks like sea
  // and the bottom half looks like sea seen from a boat. Beneath the waterline
  // the surface is a bright, tinted ceiling with the sky pouring through the
  // Snell window overhead and near-total reflection toward the horizon.
  if (!gl_FrontFacing) {
    float up = max(dot(n, viewDir), 0.0);

    // Snell's window: refraction crowds the whole sky into a ~96 degree cone
    // overhead, and outside it the surface mirrors the water. 'up' stands in for
    // the angle, so the transition lands where the physics puts it.
    float window = smoothstep(0.62, 0.82, up);

    vec3 through = mix(uDeep * 0.55, uSkyColor, window);
    float glint = pow(max(dot(reflect(-viewDir, n), uSunDir), 0.0), 90.0);
    through += uSunColor * glint * window * 1.6;

    // Denser the further the sightline runs through water, so the ceiling fades
    // out rather than ending.
    float murk = 1.0 - exp(-viewDist * 0.02);
    through = mix(through, uDeep * 0.35, murk);

    gl_FragColor = vec4(through, mix(0.35, 0.9, murk));
    return;
  }

  // SUBSURFACE SCATTERING \u2014 the Sea of Thieves colour model, and the thing that
  // was missing.
  //
  // Ang, "The Technical Art of Sea of Thieves" (SIGGRAPH 2018): the water colour
  // "is based on scattering approximations. We blend between a deep water colour
  // and a sub-surface water colour based on a combination of view angle, sun
  // direction and a wave peak mask... Where the choppiness offset is greater,
  // this corresponds to wave peaks, which show more sub-surface due to shorter
  // distance traveled by light through the water."
  //
  // So the bright tropical green-teal is not the water's albedo \u2014 it is light
  // coming THROUGH the water toward you, strongest looking into the sun and
  // strongest on the crests. Ours has no FFT choppiness to build a peak mask
  // from, so the ripple normal stands in: where it tilts toward the eye, the
  // water is standing up, which is where light gets through.
  float towardSun = max(dot(-viewDir, uSunDir), 0.0);
  float peak = clamp(ripple.x * 6.0 + ripple.y * 6.0 + 0.5, 0.0, 1.0);
  float sss = pow(towardSun, 3.0) * mix(0.15, 1.0, peak);

  // REFRACTION: what is actually behind the water, bent and drunk on the way.
  //
  // The scene was grabbed before this surface drew (see onBeforeRender), so it
  // holds the seabed and anything standing in the water. Offsetting the lookup by
  // the ripple normal is the refraction; the offset shrinks with distance because
  // a wave a kilometre away subtends less than a pixel and a fixed offset there
  // is just noise.
  vec2 screenUv = gl_FragCoord.xy * uSceneTexel;
  float bend = 22.0 * exp(-viewDist * 0.01);
  vec2 refractUv = clamp(screenUv + ripple * bend * uSceneTexel, vec2(0.001), vec2(0.999));
  vec3 behind = texture2D(uScene, refractUv).rgb;

  // Beer-Lambert again, and deliberately the same extinction the terrain uses so
  // a seabed shaded through the water agrees with a seabed shaded by it: red goes
  // first, then green, and what survives is blue.
  vec3 absorb = exp(-vec3(0.28, 0.09, 0.045) * depth);

  // Depth tint: bright shallows fading to deep blue.
  float dt = clamp(depth / 22.0, 0.0, 1.0);
  dt = dt * dt * (3.0 - 2.0 * dt);
  vec3 body = mix(uShallow, uDeep, dt);

  // The water's own colour is what the light BECOMES once the scene behind it has
  // been absorbed away \u2014 so they are not two layers to blend, they are one path:
  // what survives of the seabed, plus what the water scatters back.
  vec3 color = behind * absorb + body * (1.0 - absorb);

  // Fresnel sky reflection toward grazing angles. Schlick, with a real F0 for
  // water (0.02): the old flat 0.6 mix washed the colour out at every angle,
  // where water is almost transparent looking down and almost a mirror looking
  // along it. That contrast IS the look.
  float fres = 0.02 + 0.98 * pow(1.0 - max(dot(n, viewDir), 0.0), 5.0);
  // Scattered light rides ON the body colour, before the sky reflection, because
  // it comes from inside the water rather than off it.
  color = mix(color, uSubsurface, sss * 0.75);

  color = mix(color, uSkyColor, fres);

  // Sun glint by the closest-point-on-sphere approximation (Karis, "Real Shading
  // in Unreal Engine 4", 2013), which is what the SoT talk cites. Treating the
  // sun as a disc rather than a point is the difference between a hard pinprick
  // and the broad shimmering track a real sea has: the reflection vector is
  // pulled toward the light's centre, and anything within its angular radius
  // reflects at full strength.
  vec3 refl = reflect(-viewDir, n);
  float SUN_ANGULAR_RADIUS = 0.06;
  vec3 toCentre = uSunDir - refl * dot(refl, uSunDir);
  vec3 closest = normalize(uSunDir - toCentre * clamp(SUN_ANGULAR_RADIUS / max(length(toCentre), 1e-4), 0.0, 1.0));
  float spec = pow(max(dot(refl, closest), 0.0), 400.0);
  color += uSunColor * spec * 4.0;

  // Constant-width shoreline foam (~2.5 m along the waterline, slope-independent),
  // faded out with distance: past a few hundred metres the band is thinner than a
  // pixel, and the seabed derivatives behind it alias into the shimmer that made
  // the far sea sparkle.
  float shoreLod = exp(-viewDist * 0.004);
  float foam = smoothstep(2.5, 0.0, shoreDist) * shoreLod;
  color = mix(color, vec3(1.0), foam * 0.7);

  // Transparency: clear looking DOWN, opaque looking ALONG.
  //
  // The old ramp hit 0.9 by 4m of depth, which hid the seabed everywhere except
  // the last step of a beach \u2014 you could not see the bottom in water you were
  // standing in. Real water hides its floor because the sightline through it
  // gets long at grazing angles, not because it is deep, so the Fresnel term
  // drives opacity as well as reflection: straight down stays readable, the
  // distance stays a sea.
  // The refracted scene already carries the seabed, so transparency is no longer
  // how the bottom shows through \u2014 absorption is. What alpha still buys is the
  // soft edge where water meets land, and a touch of see-through at the shore.
  float alpha = mix(0.86, 1.0, fres);
  alpha = max(alpha, foam * 0.9);

  // Anti-aliased waterline (see edge above) \u2014 a ~1 px smooth coverage edge
  // instead of a hard jagged cutoff or a wide depth-based fade, so the shore
  // stays crisp and the foam stays visible at every shore angle.
  alpha *= edge;

  gl_FragColor = vec4(color, alpha);

  // THE SAME FOG AS THE LAND, by being the same code: a sea and a shore are in
  // the same air, and any term that differs between them shows up exactly where
  // the sea is all there is. A hand copy of the land's formula, fed by its own
  // uniforms, drifted \u2014 past a short Render Distance the land is culled and the
  // sea under it showed through as blue shapes (Nick, 2026-10-19).
  #include <fog_fragment>
}
`;

`, dL = `
uniform float uFallTime;
varying vec4 vFlow;
varying vec3 vCard;
varying vec2 vGround;
varying float vLife;

float fallHash(vec2 p) {
	return fract(sin(dot(p, vec2(127.1, 311.7))) * 43758.5453);
}

float fallNoise(vec2 p) {
	vec2 i = floor(p);
	vec2 f = fract(p);
	f = f * f * (3.0 - 2.0 * f);
	return mix(
		mix(fallHash(i), fallHash(i + vec2(1.0, 0.0)), f.x),
		mix(fallHash(i + vec2(0.0, 1.0)), fallHash(i + vec2(1.0, 1.0)), f.x),
		f.y
	);
}
`, fL = `
const vec3 FALL_DEEP = vec3(0.10, 0.42, 0.66);
const vec3 FALL_LIGHT = vec3(0.50, 0.80, 0.92);
const vec3 FALL_FOAM = vec3(0.93, 0.97, 1.0);
float kind = vFlow.w;
vec3 fallColor;
float fallAlpha;
if (kind < 0.5) {
	float across = vFlow.x;
	float tau = vFlow.y;
	float drop = vFlow.z;
	// Streak space moves down with the water: the same streak is at the same tau - time.
	float flow = tau - uFallTime;
	// Turned a little off the noise's grid, which otherwise shows as level lines across the sheet.
	const mat2 SKEW = mat2(0.94, 0.34, -0.34, 0.94);
	float streak = fallNoise(SKEW * vec2(across * 0.8, flow * 1.3));
	float rush = fallNoise(SKEW * vec2(across * 2.1 + 17.0, flow * 3.4));
	float s = streak * 0.6 + rush * 0.4;

	fallColor = mix(FALL_DEEP, FALL_LIGHT, smoothstep(0.25, 0.6, s));
	fallColor = mix(fallColor, FALL_FOAM, smoothstep(0.55, 0.78, s));
	// Glassy over the brink, the streaks only starting as it tips: a bright band at the lip.
	float brink = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.0, 0.45, abs(tau - 0.05));
	fallColor = mix(fallColor, mix(FALL_LIGHT, FALL_FOAM, 0.55), brink * 0.75);
	// It takes air as it falls, and is white water by the foot.
	fallColor = mix(fallColor, FALL_FOAM, smoothstep(0.35, 1.0, drop) * 0.7);

	fallAlpha = mix(0.72, 0.97, smoothstep(0.2, 0.7, s));
	fallAlpha = max(fallAlpha, smoothstep(0.5, 1.0, drop));
	// Ragged at the sides, and thinning as it fans out.
	float edge = abs(vCard.x) + (rush - 0.5) * 0.35 + drop * 0.12;
	fallAlpha *= 1.0 - smoothstep(0.78, 1.0, edge);
	// It slides in over the top rather than starting at a line.
	fallAlpha *= vCard.y;
} else if (kind < 1.5) {
	// Foam churning out from where it lands, thinning to the patch's edge.
	// Three octaves, each turned off the last's grid, so the foam has no square cells in it.
	float r = length(vCard.xy);
	vec2 q = vGround * 0.3;
	float churn = fallNoise(q + vec2(uFallTime * 0.3, -uFallTime * 0.2)) * 0.5;
	q = mat2(0.8, -0.6, 0.6, 0.8) * q * 2.1;
	churn += fallNoise(q - vec2(uFallTime * 0.55, uFallTime * 0.4)) * 0.3;
	q = mat2(0.8, -0.6, 0.6, 0.8) * q * 2.3;
	churn += fallNoise(q + vec2(uFallTime * 0.9, uFallTime * 0.7)) * 0.2;
	fallColor = mix(FALL_LIGHT, FALL_FOAM, smoothstep(0.3, 0.55, churn + (1.0 - r) * 0.25));
	fallAlpha = (1.0 - smoothstep(0.3, 1.0, r + (churn - 0.5) * 0.5)) * 0.95;
} else {
	float r = length(vCard.xy);
	fallColor = FALL_FOAM;
	fallAlpha = exp(-4.0 * r * r) * step(r, 1.0) * 0.6 * sin(3.14159 * vLife);
}
if (fallAlpha <= 0.002) discard;
diffuseColor = vec4(fallColor, fallAlpha);
`, pL = `
roughnessFactor = vFlow.w < 0.5 ? mix(0.5, 0.85, smoothstep(0.3, 1.0, vFlow.z)) : 0.95;
`;

		#include <common>
		#include <color_pars_vertex>
		#include <fog_pars_vertex>
		#include <logdepthbuf_pars_vertex>
		#include <clipping_planes_pars_vertex>

		uniform float linewidth;
		uniform vec2 resolution;

		attribute vec3 instanceStart;
		attribute vec3 instanceEnd;

		attribute vec3 instanceColorStart;
		attribute vec3 instanceColorEnd;

		#ifdef WORLD_UNITS

			varying vec4 worldPos;
			varying vec3 worldStart;
			varying vec3 worldEnd;

			#ifdef USE_DASH

				varying vec2 vUv;

			#endif

		#else

			varying vec2 vUv;

		#endif

		#ifdef USE_DASH

			uniform float dashScale;
			attribute float instanceDistanceStart;
			attribute float instanceDistanceEnd;
			varying float vLineDistance;

		#endif

		void trimSegment( const in vec4 start, inout vec4 end ) {

			// trim end segment so it terminates between the camera plane and the near plane

			// conservative estimate of the near plane
			float a = projectionMatrix[ 2 ][ 2 ]; // 3nd entry in 3th column
			float b = projectionMatrix[ 3 ][ 2 ]; // 3nd entry in 4th column
			float nearEstimate = - 0.5 * b / a;

			float alpha = ( nearEstimate - start.z ) / ( end.z - start.z );

			end.xyz = mix( start.xyz, end.xyz, alpha );

		}

		void main() {

			#ifdef USE_COLOR

				vColor.xyz = ( position.y < 0.5 ) ? instanceColorStart : instanceColorEnd;

			#endif

			#ifdef USE_DASH

				vLineDistance = ( position.y < 0.5 ) ? dashScale * instanceDistanceStart : dashScale * instanceDistanceEnd;
				vUv = uv;

			#endif

			float aspect = resolution.x / resolution.y;

			// camera space
			vec4 start = modelViewMatrix * vec4( instanceStart, 1.0 );
			vec4 end = modelViewMatrix * vec4( instanceEnd, 1.0 );

			#ifdef WORLD_UNITS

				worldStart = start.xyz;
				worldEnd = end.xyz;

			#else

				vUv = uv;

			#endif

			// special case for perspective projection, and segments that terminate either in, or behind, the camera plane
			// clearly the gpu firmware has a way of addressing this issue when projecting into ndc space
			// but we need to perform ndc-space calculations in the shader, so we must address this issue directly
			// perhaps there is a more elegant solution -- WestLangley

			bool perspective = ( projectionMatrix[ 2 ][ 3 ] == - 1.0 ); // 4th entry in the 3rd column

			if ( perspective ) {

				if ( start.z < 0.0 && end.z >= 0.0 ) {

					trimSegment( start, end );

				} else if ( end.z < 0.0 && start.z >= 0.0 ) {

					trimSegment( end, start );

				}

			}

			// clip space
			vec4 clipStart = projectionMatrix * start;
			vec4 clipEnd = projectionMatrix * end;

			// ndc space
			vec3 ndcStart = clipStart.xyz / clipStart.w;
			vec3 ndcEnd = clipEnd.xyz / clipEnd.w;

			// direction
			vec2 dir = ndcEnd.xy - ndcStart.xy;

			// account for clip-space aspect ratio
			dir.x *= aspect;
			dir = normalize( dir );

			#ifdef WORLD_UNITS

				vec3 worldDir = normalize( end.xyz - start.xyz );
				vec3 tmpFwd = normalize( mix( start.xyz, end.xyz, 0.5 ) );
				vec3 worldUp = normalize( cross( worldDir, tmpFwd ) );
				vec3 worldFwd = cross( worldDir, worldUp );
				worldPos = position.y < 0.5 ? start: end;

				// height offset
				float hw = linewidth * 0.5;
				worldPos.xyz += position.x < 0.0 ? hw * worldUp : - hw * worldUp;

				// don't extend the line if we're rendering dashes because we
				// won't be rendering the endcaps
				#ifndef USE_DASH

					// cap extension
					worldPos.xyz += position.y < 0.5 ? - hw * worldDir : hw * worldDir;

					// add width to the box
					worldPos.xyz += worldFwd * hw;

					// endcaps
					if ( position.y > 1.0 || position.y < 0.0 ) {

						worldPos.xyz -= worldFwd * 2.0 * hw;

					}

				#endif

				// project the worldpos
				vec4 clip = projectionMatrix * worldPos;

				// shift the depth of the projected points so the line
				// segments overlap neatly
				vec3 clipPose = ( position.y < 0.5 ) ? ndcStart : ndcEnd;
				clip.z = clipPose.z * clip.w;

			#else

				vec2 offset = vec2( dir.y, - dir.x );
				// undo aspect ratio adjustment
				dir.x /= aspect;
				offset.x /= aspect;

				// sign flip
				if ( position.x < 0.0 ) offset *= - 1.0;

				// endcaps
				if ( position.y < 0.0 ) {

					offset += - dir;

				} else if ( position.y > 1.0 ) {

					offset += dir;

				}

				// adjust for linewidth
				offset *= linewidth;

				// adjust for clip-space to screen-space conversion // maybe resolution should be based on viewport ...
				offset /= resolution.y;

				// select end
				vec4 clip = ( position.y < 0.5 ) ? clipStart : clipEnd;

				// back to clip space
				offset *= clip.w;

				clip.xy += offset;

			#endif

			gl_Position = clip;

			vec4 mvPosition = ( position.y < 0.5 ) ? start : end; // this is an approximation

			#include <logdepthbuf_vertex>
			#include <clipping_planes_vertex>
			#include <fog_vertex>

		}
		`,
    fragmentShader: `
		uniform vec3 diffuse;
		uniform float opacity;
		uniform float linewidth;

		#ifdef USE_DASH

			uniform float dashOffset;
			uniform float dashSize;
			uniform float gapSize;

		#endif

		varying float vLineDistance;

		#ifdef WORLD_UNITS

			varying vec4 worldPos;
			varying vec3 worldStart;
			varying vec3 worldEnd;

			#ifdef USE_DASH

				varying vec2 vUv;

			#endif

		#else

			varying vec2 vUv;

		#endif

		#include <common>
		#include <color_pars_fragment>
		#include <fog_pars_fragment>
		#include <logdepthbuf_pars_fragment>
		#include <clipping_planes_pars_fragment>

		vec2 closestLineToLine(vec3 p1, vec3 p2, vec3 p3, vec3 p4) {

			float mua;
			float mub;

			vec3 p13 = p1 - p3;
			vec3 p43 = p4 - p3;

			vec3 p21 = p2 - p1;

			float d1343 = dot( p13, p43 );
			float d4321 = dot( p43, p21 );
			float d1321 = dot( p13, p21 );
			float d4343 = dot( p43, p43 );
			float d2121 = dot( p21, p21 );

			float denom = d2121 * d4343 - d4321 * d4321;

			float numer = d1343 * d4321 - d1321 * d4343;

			mua = numer / denom;
			mua = clamp( mua, 0.0, 1.0 );
			mub = ( d1343 + d4321 * ( mua ) ) / d4343;
			mub = clamp( mub, 0.0, 1.0 );

			return vec2( mua, mub );

		}

		void main() {

			float alpha = opacity;
			vec4 diffuseColor = vec4( diffuse, alpha );

			#include <clipping_planes_fragment>

			#ifdef USE_DASH

				if ( vUv.y < - 1.0 || vUv.y > 1.0 ) discard; // discard endcaps

				if ( mod( vLineDistance + dashOffset, dashSize + gapSize ) > dashSize ) discard; // todo - FIX

			#endif

			#ifdef WORLD_UNITS

				// Find the closest points on the view ray and the line segment
				vec3 rayEnd = normalize( worldPos.xyz ) * 1e5;
				vec3 lineDir = worldEnd - worldStart;
				vec2 params = closestLineToLine( worldStart, worldEnd, vec3( 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 ), rayEnd );

				vec3 p1 = worldStart + lineDir * params.x;
				vec3 p2 = rayEnd * params.y;
				vec3 delta = p1 - p2;
				float len = length( delta );
				float norm = len / linewidth;

				#ifndef USE_DASH

					#ifdef USE_ALPHA_TO_COVERAGE

						float dnorm = fwidth( norm );
						alpha = 1.0 - smoothstep( 0.5 - dnorm, 0.5 + dnorm, norm );

					#else

						if ( norm > 0.5 ) {

							discard;

						}

					#endif

				#endif

			#else

				#ifdef USE_ALPHA_TO_COVERAGE

					// artifacts appear on some hardware if a derivative is taken within a conditional
					float a = vUv.x;
					float b = ( vUv.y > 0.0 ) ? vUv.y - 1.0 : vUv.y + 1.0;
					float len2 = a * a + b * b;
					float dlen = fwidth( len2 );

					if ( abs( vUv.y ) > 1.0 ) {

						alpha = 1.0 - smoothstep( 1.0 - dlen, 1.0 + dlen, len2 );

					}

				#else

					if ( abs( vUv.y ) > 1.0 ) {

						float a = vUv.x;
						float b = ( vUv.y > 0.0 ) ? vUv.y - 1.0 : vUv.y + 1.0;
						float len2 = a * a + b * b;

						if ( len2 > 1.0 ) discard;

					}

				#endif

			#endif

			#include <logdepthbuf_fragment>
			#include <color_fragment>

			gl_FragColor = vec4( diffuseColor.rgb, alpha );

			#include <tonemapping_fragment>
			#include <colorspace_fragment>
			#include <fog_fragment>
			#include <premultiplied_alpha_fragment>

		}
		`
